topics.title: Causative Construction (Faire + Infinitif & Se Faire + Infinitif)
topics.objective: Master the causative structure (*faire* + infinitive, *se faire* + infinitive) to express causing an action to be performed by someone else, managing word order, pronoun placement before *faire*, and introducing agents with *par* or *à*.

topics.title: Concordance and Sequence of Tenses in Subordinate Clauses (La Concordance des Temps)
topics.objective: Apply the correct tense shifts (sequence of tenses / concordance des temps) in subordinate clauses based on the tense of the main reporting clause across direct/indirect speech and complex sentence structures.

topics.title: Infinitive Negation & Word Order (Ne pas, Ne jamais, Ne plus + Infinitif)
topics.objective: Form negated infinitive clauses correctly by placing negative adverbial pairs (*ne pas*, *ne jamais*, *ne plus*, *ne rien*) immediately before the infinitive verb, while positioning object and reflexive pronouns between the negative pair and the infinitive.

topics.title: Introduction to the Subjunctive Mood (Le Subjonctif Présent)
topics.objective: Understand the fundamental mood distinction between indicative objective reality and subjunctive subjective reality, master the 5 core trigger categories, and apply regular stem formation rules (-e, -es, -e, -ions, -iez, -ent) as the gateway to B2 advanced subjunctive structures.

topics.title: Impersonal Expressions: General Infinitive (de + inf) vs Specific Subjunctive (que + subjonctif)
topics.objective: Distinguish and master impersonal expressions (*il est possible*, *il vaut mieux*, *il est important*, *il s'agit de*, *il convient de*) contrasting general statements using *de* + infinitive against specific-subject subclauses using *que* + subjunctive.

topics.title: The French Gerund (Le Gérondif: En + Participe Présent) & Adjectival Participle Distinction
topics.objective: Form the French gerund (`en` + present participle stem `-ant`), master its adverbial functions (simultaneity, manner/means, condition, cause), enforce the strict subject co-referentiality constraint, and distinguish the invariant verbal gerund/participle from the variable verbal adjective (*adjectif verbal*).
